C-ATTEMPT-LOG.Summary: Record every attempt (not only outcomes) on the run ledger, keep a dumb fix budget of 2, escalate to paused-pending-approval rather than abort, and make attempt fields survive fold — with a kind vocabulary, an incomplete-epoch mark, and a report-only cursor attempt surface.
C-ATTEMPT-LOG.Problem:
Phase 3 shipped the ledger and cursor; Phase 4 is where the track's subject — the record that makes a confident report about unchecked work detectable — is supposed to land. Measured at 235f0f8 and re-verified at 471f06b (A5.5), three facts make the phase as written unbuildable:
1. The fold destroys the attempt payload (A18.2 / correction 31). LooseEvent is { id, task, kind, file, allocations? } (grace-cursor.ts:102-108); listLooseEvents reads no attempt attributes (listLooseEvents:127); buildEpochNode emits a three-attribute Event literal (grace-cursor.ts:752-761). An outcome and a FailureSignature written on a loose event are gone at epoch close. D9's "same failure twice vs two different failures" and D6's calibration join depend on exactly those fields.
2. Escalation cannot fold (A18.3 / correction 32). validateEventsAgainstAllocations:727-730 and foldEpoch:308-311 refuse a used range with no terminal event. §4.4 routes exhaustion to paused-pending-approval via pause, which is not range-terminating. Attempt events for the runs that went worst stay loose while clean runs land in the ledger — correlated loss of the kind D6 On loss names. Separately, §3.4's complete/incomplete mark was never built: no complete attribute exists on any Epoch node.
3. Event kinds are free strings (A18.4 / correction 33). advance --kind atempt folds clean; budget accounting keys on the string, so a typo resets the counter silently (anti-pattern 8).
Step 4.5.1 says "record on every verification cycle," but nothing in the binary runs one (A18.6 / correction 35): ngrace verification is find/show only. The only actor that knows an attempt happened is the executing agent; the surface it calls is a design decision, answered by A18.11 as ngrace cursor attempt (report-only; never blocks — anti-pattern 9).
§4.3 names src/artifact/types.ts as the home of run-state types; they live in grace-cursor.ts:35-108. The field registry of A18.7 is the one thing that belongs in artifact/types.ts, beside the companion registry it copies (A18.5 / correction 34).

Goals.Goal: Typed attempt fields (outcome, ordinal, optional failure signature, write-evidence digest) behind one exported field registry read by listLooseEvents, buildEpochNode, and validateLedgerEpoch — so a field added once survives a fold without re-listing at three sites (A18.7, A19.1).
Attempt outcome and failure signature present in run-ledger.xml after a fold, asserted on the folded ledger and not only on the loose event (A18.2).

Escalation emits a range-terminating event so the exhausted task's epoch folds; the task is paused-pending-approval in the cursor (task state, not epoch state). fold gains Epoch-N complete="false" for the genuinely incomplete case as an explicit act; default remains refuse (A18.8, A7.2 both-directions).
Known event-kind vocabulary; ledger.unknown-event-kind fires as a warning on unregistered kinds; no new error on previously-green projects (A18.9, invariant 5).

Dumb fix budget of 2 (FIX_BUDGET named constant with D9 judgment note). Every attempt counts regardless of signature. Budget spans folds: two failures split by an epoch close still exhaust it (A18.12 §2). Exhaustion is a normal state, not a failure (D9).

ngrace cursor attempt --change C-* --task T-* --outcome pass|fail [--signature-kind K --signature-key S]: allocates ordinal, records the attempt, accounts the budget, transitions on exhaustion, prints both signatures. Reports; never refuses the next attempt (A18.11, anti-pattern 9). Gates that refuse are Phase 5.

Flake classification as a pure read over the log comparing write-evidence digests recorded on consecutive attempts (A19.1 / correction 36). fail→pass with identical recorded digests is flaky; different digests is normal-retry; absent or unrecordable evidence is unable-to-determine with a reason from verdicts.md — never "normal retry" (A18.10). Evidence is content-sensitive (digest over path+content-hash pairs of scope-intersecting files at record time), not a file list. No commands are run.
Exhaustion visible on a human surface (status prints paused/exhausted tasks) so a correct continuous signal is not functionally equivalent to no signal (A18.12 §3, A17.2).

Constraints.Constraint: A18.7–A18.11 are ratified. Do not re-open them and do not invent a sixth decision. On contradiction, report and stop (§12.5; Correction 26 / A13.1 is the precedent).
The counter stays dumb (D9). No logic may decide an attempt "was progress" and should not count. The signature is for the escalation message and analysis only.
FIX_BUDGET = 2 is a named constant with the "judgment, not derived" note from D9 beside it. Churn is recorded; calibration later may revise the number.
Mechanisms report; they do not block (anti-pattern 9, A18.11). cursor attempt never refuses a further attempt. Refusing is a gate (Phase 5, D11, D14).
Additive only. A project with no attempts, no exhaustion, and no incomplete epochs lints clean. ledger.unknown-event-kind is warning severity so invariant 5 holds (A18.9, §0.7.4).

No timestamps in attempt identity or ordering. Ordering is by allocated event id range (D2, §0.2, anti-pattern 6). Ordinal is 1-based within the task, allocated as max existing attempt-ordinal for that task across ledger and loose + 1 at write time (same span as nextEventId:903-907). Concurrent attempt recording on the same task is unsupported; attempt is sequential per task under D9's write-plus-verification definition. The statement has a witness: ledger.duplicate-attempt-ordinal (error) fires when two attempt events share (task, ordinal) (A19.2 / correction 37). Safe under invariant 5 because only this phase's attempt kind can trigger it.

Field registry lives in src/artifact/types.ts beside NGRACE_CHANGE_BUNDLE_COMPANIONS. Run-state types (CursorState, LooseEvent, …) stay in grace-cursor.ts; do not relocate them into artifact/types.ts (A18.5).

complete="false" is an explicit fold act (e.g. --allow-incomplete). Default fold still refuses holes and unterminated ranges. ledger.range-unterminated and ledger.range-hole keep firing on epochs not marked incomplete, and must not fire on ones that are (A18.8, A7.2).
Escalation's range-terminating event is a registered kind (exhausted) recognized as terminal for density/membership checks; pause alone remains non-terminating.
Skill text: when to record an attempt and when to escalate — one or two sentences. Never restate codes the binary emits (anti-pattern 10, D13).
Every new issue code registers with derivedFrom and proposedBy (§12.1) and has integration tests both directions (§0.2, A12.2). Do not add to Phase 3's unit-only debt.
skills/ngrace/* is source of truth; plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/* stays byte-identical in the same commit (invariant 1, §12.2).
No new runtime dependencies. No Phase 5+ constructs: no gate surface, no reviewer, no claimed-confidence field (Phase 9), no doctor repair.
AffectedAreas is derived by tracing real surfaces (A18.5 table plus findings), never transcribed from §4.3 (A5.6, A11.7).
Shared test helpers live in src/test-support/; production modules must not import them (invariant 7).

NonGoals.NonGoal: Transition gates and the third check surface (Phase 5; D11, D12, D14).
Marker-divergence failure localization beyond the flake read (Phase 7 / D8 remainder).
claimed-confidence and the calibration report (Phase 9; D6 calibration half).
Blocking further attempts after budget exhaustion (that is a gate; Phase 5).
Making the ledger a free-form attribute bag; typed fields only (A18.7 rejected alt).
Overloading advance --kind attempt as the attempt surface (A18.11 rejected alt).
Storing flake classification as a ledger verdict; it is a derived read (A18.10).
Lint validation of loose run/ event files (A11.2; fold and attempt own it).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-SURVIVES-FOLD: An attempt recorded with outcome and (on fail) signature-kind and signature-key is present with those fields intact in run-ledger.xml after foldEpoch (A18.2). Assertion is on the folded Event node attributes, not on the loose file. Reproduced pre-fix shape at HEAD: only id, task, kind survive today (grace-cursor.ts:752-761). Discriminating negative: a test that writes outcome="fail" signature-kind="test-failure" signature-key="x" and fails if the folded Event lacks any of those attributes.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EVENT-FIELD-REGISTRY: One exported constant in src/artifact/types.ts maps typed event fields (kind → attribute name → validator) and is the sole source listLooseEvents, buildEpochNode, and validateLedgerEpoch read for those fields (A18.7). Discriminating negative: a unit test that adds a field to the registry only and asserts it survives a fold without editing the three consumer sites. Without that test the registry is three literals wearing a constant's name.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EPOCH-COMPLETENESS: (a) Escalation via cursor attempt on the second failure emits a range-terminating exhausted event; the epoch folds; cursor task state is paused (paused-pending-approval semantics) (A18.8 half 1). (b) fold with an explicit incomplete act writes Epoch-N complete="false" and succeeds for a used range with a hole or no terminal event; default fold still refuses those cases (A18.8 half 2). (c) Both-directions table for complete="false" (A7.2): ledger.range-unterminated and ledger.range-hole fire on epochs not marked complete="false" and do not fire on ones that are; existing refuse-before-write negatives still fail closed. (d) Range-terminating set membership table (A19.3 / correction 38): an epoch closed by exhausted folds; an epoch whose only closing event is pause still refuses; an epoch closed by an unregistered kind still refuses and emits ledger.unknown-event-kind when that kind is present on a written ledger. A15's refuse-before-write negatives must still fail closed — a widened set must not disarm them.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-UNKNOWN-KIND-WARNING: Known kinds are registered (opened, progress, pause, resume, terminal, attempt, exhausted at minimum). An Event with an unregistered kind produces ledger.unknown-event-kind at warning severity, with derivedFrom and proposedBy: "confidently-wrong" (A18.9). Compat sweep (§0.7.4, A9) across polyglotFixture, minimalTsFixture, scaleFixture(20), examples/, and bun run ngrace lint --path . shows no new error code anywhere; the warning does not appear on clean fixtures that never author ad-hoc kinds.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FLAKE-THREE-OUTCOMES: Amended by A19.1 / correction 36, A20.1 / correction 39, and A21.1 / correction 44 (A13.3 — criterion corrected in the artifact, not redefined in the diff). At record time, cursor attempt stamps a write-evidence attribute (registry field, A18.7): a content-sensitive digest that folds (1) git rev-parse HEAD and (2) sorted (path, content-hash) pairs for ObservedWriteScope ∩ currently-changed files — or omits the field when evidence is unrecordable. Unavailable paths (each → unable-to-determine): no active scope; git status non-zero; git HEAD unresolvable including unborn HEAD after git init with no commit (A21.1 — a failed measurement must not become HEAD:""). Committed movement between attempts moves the digest; an empty worktree intersection is not "nothing happened" when HEAD is resolvable (A20.1). Classification is a pure read comparing consecutive recorded digests on the most recent fail→pass pair (A20.3) — never re-queries the live worktree for the between-attempts answer. Discriminating tests: different recorded evidence → normal-retry after worktree clean; fix committed between attempts → normal-retry (A20.1); identical evidence (same HEAD, same uncommitted digests) → flaky; absent or unrecordable write-evidence including unborn HEAD → unable-to-determine with a reason from verdicts.md — never normal-retry or flaky. Two fail→pass pairs: most recent wins (A20.3). Boundary (A21.2, not a defect): an uncommitted fix outside ObservedWriteScope does not move the digest, so fail→pass around it reads as flaky — the scope defines what this change may write; Phase 7 must know what the signal does not cover. Classification is never a stored verdict field. No commands run.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-BUDGET-SPANS-FOLD: Two failed attempts on the same task, with a successful fold between them, still exhaust FIX_BUDGET on the second failure (A18.12 §2). Counter reads attempt events across run-ledger.xml and run/ (same shape as nextEventId / maxLedgerEventId). A counter that reads only run/ is a defect. Discriminating negative for "stays dumb": two failures with different signatures still exhaust (step 4.5.2 / D9).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-SURFACE: ngrace cursor attempt is registered beside show/regenerate/advance/pause/resume/fold (A18.11). It allocates ordinal, writes the attempt event with registry fields, updates budget accounting, on exhaustion writes the range-terminating exhausted event and paused cursor state, and prints both failure signatures. Exit is success (non-blocking) even on exhaustion. A third attempt after exhaustion still records; it does not refuse. advance --kind attempt is not the attempt surface and does not perform budget policy.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXHAUSTION-SURFACE: ngrace status surfaces paused/exhausted tasks so a human can see budget exhaustion without reading the ledger by hand (A18.12 §3). formatStatusText and JSON both carry it (A5.4). The signal survives fold: listPausedTasks reads ledger exhausted/pause events not later cleared by resume/terminal, and foldEpoch must not overwrite paused with idle (A20.2). Integration test in grace-status.test.ts asserts formatStatusText contains paused= after an exhausted fold — not only a unit assertion against collectProjectStatus (A20.5). chooseNextAction does not consult the cursor (anti-pattern 7, A10.8).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DROP-SITE-INVENTORY: A5.4 inventory in the phase report for LooseEvent, buildEpochNode, validateLedgerEpoch / parseLedgerEvent, writeEventFile, and ChangeBundleStatus / formatStatusText: each site marked widened, deliberately not widened with reason, or not on the path. No new field may be introduced by re-listing field names at a fourth site outside the registry.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CATALOG-AND-INTEGRATION: Every new issue code is an exact catalog entry with derivedFrom and proposedBy (§12.1): ledger.unknown-event-kind (warning, A18.9) and ledger.duplicate-attempt-ordinal (error, A19.2). Each has one integration test that it fires and one that it does not fire on a clean project (§0.2, A12.2). Unit-only coverage is not sufficient.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ADDITIVE: Invariant 5 demonstrated, not asserted: polyglotFixture(), minimalTsFixture(), scaleFixture(20), examples/, and bun run ngrace lint --path . each yield zero new error codes (§0.7.4, A9). A new error on a previously-green project is release-breaking.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DOCS-AND-SKILLS: The attempt subcommand reaches its callers: README.md command table and output-format list; skills/ngrace/ngrace-cli/SKILL.md surface list; skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md states when to record attempts and when to escalate (budget of 2 → replan) in one or two sentences, never restating codes (D13, anti-pattern 10). Both packaged mirrors byte-identical in the same commit (§12.2). Token delta reported (§0.5, D15). M-CURSOR summary updated for the seventh subcommand.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/grace-cursor.test.ts src/artifact/grammar.test.ts src/grace-lint.test.ts src/grace-status.test.ts src/lint/catalog.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Folded-ledger assertion that attempt outcome and signature attributes survive fold (AC-ATTEMPT-SURVIVES-FOLD). Registry add-a-field test touching only the constant (AC-EVENT-FIELD-REGISTRY). Both-directions table for complete="false" vs refuse (AC-EPOCH-COMPLETENESS, A7.2). Warning-only unknown-kind on a typo kind and clean compat sweep including bun run ngrace lint --path . (AC-UNKNOWN-KIND-WARNING, A9). Three flake outcomes each tested against recorded digests, including worktree-clean normal-retry and both unable-to-determine paths (AC-FLAKE-THREE-OUTCOMES, A19.1). Two failures split by fold still exhaust; two different signatures still exhaust (AC-BUDGET-SPANS-FOLD). cursor attempt non-blocking after exhaustion (AC-ATTEMPT-SURFACE). Status surfaces exhaustion (AC-EXHAUSTION-SURFACE). A5.4 drop-site inventory (AC-DROP-SITE-INVENTORY). Integration both-directions per new code including ledger.duplicate-attempt-ordinal (AC-CATALOG-AND-INTEGRATION, A19.2). Range-terminating set membership table: exhausted folds, pause-only refuses, unregistered closing kind refuses and warns (A19.3). Full §0.7 self-review with all five audits; mutation check covers each production change not a sample (A14.4); adversarial probe ≥15 new inputs tagged new vs case-table (A14.6); each audit names its artifact path. Token delta (D15). Verbatim command output (A15.3). Amended criteria shown verbatim with evidence (A19.5).

Assumptions.Assumption: Phase 3 COMPLETE; ledger, fold, and cursor exist at HEAD 471f06b. A18 measurements at 235f0f8 re-verified by direct inspection at 471f06b: LooseEvent three fields, buildEpochNode three-attribute Event, terminal-only range termination, no Epoch complete attribute, no kind vocabulary, verification find/show only, run-state types in grace-cursor.ts not artifact/types.ts. bun run validate:ci exits 0 at authoring time.
A18 supersedes §4.3 and §4.5 wherever they disagree. A18.7–A18.11 are closed decisions. Standing rules A5.4, A5.5, A5.6, A7.2, A12.2, A12.3, A12.4, A14.6, A17.3 bind this phase.

Range-terminating kinds for membership checks are terminal and exhausted. pause remains non-terminating. If implementation finds a cleaner single-kind design that still satisfies A18.8's both-directions table, report it before substituting.
Exhaustion status surface is an extension of the existing epochs=/tasks= line on ChangeBundleStatus (grace-status.ts:376-379), not a new subcommand.
Path-only modules without LINKS remain warning-level and deliberate; existing graph.module-without-linked-files warnings are the expected clean state.
